title: Weighted raffle — add ticket, remove ticket, getRandom in O(1)
label: single
statement: LinkedIn is running a fair. A good action earns a member **one ticket**; a bad action **takes one ticket away**. Implement `AddTicket(memberId)`, `RemoveTicket(memberId)` and `GetRandom()`, where `GetRandom` picks a member with probability proportional to their tickets (5 tickets vs 1 ticket → 5× as likely). **All three must be O(1) on average.**
provenance: In your recent LinkedIn list (Oct 2026): "LinkedIn has organised a fair… addTicket(memberId), removeTicket(memberId) and getRandom() — weighted by tickets, all O(1) average." Closest LeetCode: 381 (Insert Delete GetRandom O(1) — duplicates allowed). InterviewDB Q12 is the same family. Stage 2 (thread safety) is the follow-up every LinkedIn data-structure question ends on.

1.a: A uniform pick over tickets is a weighted pick over members — no prefix sums needed.

1.q: RemoveTicket the last ticket in the list?
1.a: The "moved" ticket is the removed one: update the set before deleting, or handle pos == last.

2.a: O(1) average for all three; O(total tickets) memory.

2.q: Memory per member instead of per ticket?
2.a: Then picks need prefix sums: a Fenwick tree gives O(log n) for everything.

3.a: Each operation touches two structures, so one lock around each; Random is not thread-safe either.

4.a: Shard by member; pick a shard by its total tickets, then pick inside it — two-level weighting.

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: LinkedIn is running a fair. A good action earns a member **one ticket**; a bad action **takes one ticket away**. Implement `AddTicket(memberId)`, `RemoveTicket(memberId)` and `GetRandom()`, where `GetRandom` picks a member with probability proportional to their tickets (5 tickets vs 1 ticket → 5× as likely). **All three must be O(1) on average.**

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- RemoveTicket for a member with no tickets? (Return false.)
- GetRandom with no tickets at all? (Return -1.)
- Exact proportional probability? (Yes.)
- Can counts get large (millions of tickets)? (Yes — memory per ticket must be O(1).)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: Make every **ticket** an entry in a list. A uniform pick over tickets is then automatically weighted by member. Removing a ticket from the middle is O(1) if you swap the last ticket into the hole — so remember, per member, the positions of their tickets.

learn.title: 10 · Tests
learn.md:
**S1 — O(1) weighted raffle**

- empty
- remove one of two tickets of the SAME member (the moved ticket is theirs too)
- member 7 holds 5
- member 9 holds 1
- 5 : 1 weighting — 7 picked … of 60,000 (≈ 50,000)
- remove one of 7's
- 7 now holds 4
- remove from someone with none
- remove 9's only ticket
- 9 has none
- only 7 can be picked now
- 800,000 operations in … ms (< 2000 — O(1) each)

**S2 — Many threads**

- every member has exactly 10,000 tickets left

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- A prefix-sum array + binary search: O(log n) picks and O(n) updates.
- Removing from the middle of the list (O(n)).
- Forgetting to update the moved ticket's position in its owner's set.
- Removing the last ticket itself (the moved ticket is the removed one).
- The last ticket belonging to the SAME member: update their position set in the wrong order and they silently lose a second ticket — my own first version did this.
